bosnia.label: Habsburg / Austria–Hungary
bosnia.why: Annexation 5-7 Oct 1908 (Wikipedia; Hrvatska enciklopedija 1908), recognised by the Ottomans in Feb 1909 and by the powers afterwards (Bosnian crisis, but no change of holder on the ground). End 1918: governor's term ended 3 Nov 1918 and the Kingdom of SCS was formed 1 Dec 1918 (Wikipedia gives 1 Dec 1918 as the end of rule); Hrvatska enciklopedija says 1918. Same year. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/bosna-i-hercegovina

bosnia.label: Yugoslavia
bosnia.polity: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, then Yugoslavia
bosnia.why: Bosnia entered the new Yugoslav state in 1918 (Hrvatska enciklopedija; Wikipedia Austro-Hungarian rule gives 1 Dec 1918 for the end of rule). End: Yugoslavia invaded 6 April 1941 and Bosnia was included in the NDH after the capitulation on 17 April 1941 (Hrvatska enciklopedija). Both in the same year. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/bosna-i-hercegovina

bosnia.label: Yugoslavia
bosnia.polity: Yugoslavia — the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina
bosnia.why: Bosnia became a republic in postwar Yugoslavia, with the third ZAVNOBiH session in Sarajevo in April 1945 (Hrvatska enciklopedija); end: independence referendum 29 Feb-1 Mar 1992, declaration 3 March 1992, recognition 6 April (Wikipedia) or 7 April 1992 (Hrvatska enciklopedija), all in one year. The tail of the era saw rival bodies set up (Herzeg-Bosnia 18 Nov 1991; Republic of the Serbian People 9 Jan 1992), but control of the ground did not change until the war. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/bosna-i-hercegovina

campania.label: Naples / the Two Sicilies
campania.why: Ferdinand restored by the Treaty of Casalanza 20 May 1815 (Tolentino 2 or 3 May; Congress of Vienna 9 Jun 1815), but the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies is created only on 8 Dec 1816 (Wikipedia Two Sicilies and Naples infoboxes; Treccani: 1816). De facto restoration 1815 versus de jure union 1816 is a gap of about 19 months. FIX: polity for 1815-1816 should read Kingdom of Naples (restored Bourbon); 'Two Sicilies' from 8 Dec 1816. The final months 1860-61 (Naples taken 7 Sep 1860, Gaeta held by Francis II until 13 Feb 1861) are covered by the approx flag on 1861.

campania.label: Italy
campania.why: Garibaldi landed in Calabria 19 Aug 1860 and took Reggio 21 Aug (Expedition of the Thousand); plebiscite 21 Oct 1860 and annexation decree 17 Dec 1860 (Dickinson House Divided, citing Wambaugh); Gaeta capitulated 13 Feb 1861 and Civitella del Tronto 20 Mar 1861; Kingdom of Italy proclaimed 17 Mar 1861. The change of sovereignty ran Aug 1860 to Mar 1861. Kingdom of Italy sovereignty continued through WWII (Allied military government administered, Badoglio government at Brindisi), so not treated as contested.

campania.label: Italy
campania.why: 1946: referendum 2 Jun, provisional result 10 Jun, Umberto II left 13 Jun, Court of Cassation final result 18 Jun; Constitution in force 1 Jan 1948. One clean year for the change to a republic; monarchist appeals were rejected 12 to 7, no rival authority. FIX: the label 'Provincia di Caserta' fits Caserta/Arienzo (province re-established 1945, current form 1970) but Naples is not in it and Arpaia is not in Caserta's municipality list on Wikipedia (it is in Benevento province; not independently verified).

cape.label: Dutch — the Company and the Batavian Republic
cape.polity: Dutch East India Company — Cape of Good Hope
cape.why: Dutch settlement at the Cape founded April 1652 (van Riebeeck); that is a founding date, not control of the district. For the eastern ground this is far earlier than any control: the Great Fish River was agreed as the boundary only in 1780 (Wikipedia: many Xhosa already lived west of it), and the Graaff-Reinet magistracy dates from 1786. FIX: for the eastern Cape the Dutch era effectively begins about 1780-1786, not 1652; the earlier ground was held by Khoikhoi and Xhosa polities.

cape.label: Britain and its colonies
cape.why: Union of South Africa came into existence 31 May 1910; Cape Colony ended then. Later wars east of the Fish are outside this ring.

cape.label: South Africa
cape.why: Republic of South Africa 31 May 1961. Ciskei (nominal independence 4 Dec 1981 to 27 Apr 1994, unrecognised) lay east of this ring's towns; Graaff-Reinet, Cradock and Somerset East are not in it, though the ring's eastern edge near 26.5-27E is marginal.

civil-croatia.polity: Kingdom of Croatia under the Habsburg monarchy

civil-croatia.label: Yugoslavia
civil-croatia.polity: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, then Yugoslavia

england.label: Britain and its colonies
england.why: Cromwell's injunction to keep registers is dated 5 Sept 1538 (Wikipedia), but a search found other sources giving 29 Sept 1538 for publication, compliance was uneven, and it was repeated in 1547 and reaffirmed in 1597; this is a record-keeping start, not a change of sovereignty. England under Henry VIII governed through Cromwell as Vicar General, no rival authority reported.

england.label: Britain and its colonies
england.why: Civil registration began 1 July 1837 (Wikipedia GRO; several family-history sites agree; one source cites 1 March 1837 as the Act's commencement, registration itself started 1 July). Registration became compulsory only in 1874/75 (Wikipedia says 1875, other sources the 1874 Act), which the era note already says. No rival authority.

frankfurt.label: Napoleonic order — Principality, then Grand Duchy, of Frankfurt
frankfurt.polity: Napoleonic order — Principality, then Grand Duchy, of Frankfurt
frankfurt.why: the Grand Duchy ended in 1813 and the city was restored in 1815; the years between are not described

hesse-darmstadt.why: a lower bound: the Landgraviate of Hesse-Darmstadt existed before 1806, and the source gives no start

hungary.label: Habsburg / Austria–Hungary
hungary.why: Treaty of Karlowitz 26 Jan 1699; Buda had been retaken in 1686; the Banat of Temesvar stayed Ottoman until the Treaty of Passarowitz 1718, and Transylvania was nominally independent under Austrian governors (Wikipedia). No competing claimant for the post-1699 core.

hungary.label: Hungary
hungary.why: Compromise ratified by the restored Hungarian Diet 29 May 1867, Franz Joseph crowned King of Hungary 8 June 1867 (Wikipedia). It restored the pre-1848 constitution only partly; the 1848 April Laws were a prior step.

hungary.label: Hungary
hungary.why: German occupation March 1944; Szalasi's Arrow Cross government (Oct 1944) and Miklos's provisional government (28 Dec 1944) each claimed to be legitimate while the Soviets set up a separate Provisional National Government in Debrecen (22 Dec 1944); armistice 20 Jan 1945, Budapest fell 13 Feb, German troops expelled 4 April 1945. The People's Republic dates from 1949 (Wikipedia), a republic from 1946.

hungary.label: Hungary
hungary.why: Wikipedia dates the People's Republic 1949-1989 and the Third Republic 1989-2012, but free elections were 1990 and Soviet troops left 1991, so the transition was gradual. Sovereignty did not change.

istria-central.label: Habsburg / Austria–Hungary
istria-central.why: Two independent sources give 1374 for the Habsburg takeover of the Pazin County: Wikipedia Pazin (Albert III of Gorizia bequeathed the Mitterburg estates; attached to Carniola) and Hrvatska enciklopedija (Istra: Pazin county to the Habsburgs 1374 by inheritance treaty). Wikipedia notes a brief Venetian conquest 1508-09 (War of Cambrai); not a change of sovereign.

istria-central.label: Napoleonic — Illyrian Provinces
istria-central.why: Dates contradicted for THIS ground. Pazin was Austrian (not Venetian) Istria. Hrvatska enciklopedija: after Pressburg 1805 only former VENETIAN Istria went to the Kingdom of Italy; the rest of Istria went to Napoleon by Schönbrunn (14 Oct 1809) and the whole peninsula joined the Illyrian Provinces in 1809. Wikipedia Illyrian Provinces lists the March of Istria among the 1809 cessions. Austrian return: army entered Oct 1813, Treaty of Paris 1814 (Hrvatska); Wikipedia Istria says 1814; so end year is also approximate. Wikipedia Pazin does not cover the Napoleonic period.

istria-central.label: Habsburg / Austria–Hungary
istria-central.why: Start is approximate: Austria re-entered Istria Oct 1813, Treaty of Paris 1814 (Hrvatska enciklopedija), Wikipedia Istria dates the Austrian section 1814-1918; Congress of Vienna 1815. Polity label is anachronistic: Wikipedia Istria has Istria in the Kingdom of Illyria 1816-1849 (Friuli-Venezia Giulia article: Illyria abolished 1849, Austrian Littoral/Küstenland after); 'Austria-Hungary' only from 1867.

istria-central.label: Italy
istria-central.why: Italy held Istria by end 1918 after Villa Giusti armistice (3 Nov 1918; Wikipedia Treaty of Rapallo) but the formal transfer is Rapallo, 12 Nov 1920 (Wikipedia; Hrvatska says 'formally confirmed 1920'). The State of SCS laid a competing claim to the eastern Adriatic 1918-20, but Italy held Istria on the ground.

istria-central.label: Yugoslavia
istria-central.why: Yugoslav partisans took most of Istria in 1945 and entered Pazin in May 1945 (Wikipedia Istria, Pazin); the Morgan Line (June 1945) put most of Istria in Yugoslav-administered Zone B (Wikipedia Morgan Line); Italy's cession is the Paris treaty, signed 10 Feb 1947, in force 15 Sept 1947. So 1945 de facto vs 1947 de jure. No Allied enclave in central Istria.

istria-central.label: Croatia
istria-central.why: Croatia declared independence 25 June 1991, moratorium, ties severed 8 Oct 1991, EEC recognition 15 Jan 1992 (Wikipedia Independence of Croatia); the JNA withdrew from Istria 6 Dec 1991 (Hrvatska enciklopedija). No fighting in Istria is described.

istria-south.label: Republic of Venice
istria-south.polity: Republic of Venice — Istria da Mar
istria-south.why: Pula to Venice 1331 (Wikipedia Pula; Hrvatska enciklopedija), held until 1797. But Rovinj was Venetian from 1283 (Wikipedia Rovinj; Hrvatska: 'Rovinj i Piran 1283', also 1331), so 1331 is a Pula date, not region-wide.

istria-south.label: Habsburg / Austria–Hungary
istria-south.why: Campo Formio 17 Oct 1797 gives Istria to Austria (Hrvatska enciklopedija; Wikipedia Pula 1797). End is approximate: Pressburg signed 26 Dec 1805 (Wikipedia) but Istria incorporated into Kingdom of Italy 1806 (Wikipedia Istria: 1806-1810).

istria-south.label: Napoleonic — Illyrian Provinces
istria-south.why: Contradicted label. Kingdom of Italy included Istria from the Pressburg treaty (26 Dec 1805; annexation announced 30 Mar 1806, ratified 1 May 1806) until it was ceded to France under Schönbrunn (14 Oct 1809), effective 10 June 1810 (Wikipedia Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy); Hrvatska enciklopedija: 1805-1809 Kingdom of Italy, 1809 Illyrian Provinces. Austria returned Oct 1813 / 1814 (Hrvatska).

istria-south.label: Habsburg / Austria–Hungary
istria-south.why: Start approximate: Austrian army entered Istria Oct 1813, Treaty of Paris 1814 (Hrvatska enciklopedija); Wikipedia Pula says 1813, Istria/Poreč pages 1814, Umag page 1815. Label 'Küstenland' is anachronistic before 1849 (Kingdom of Illyria 1816-49, Wikipedia Istria).

istria-south.label: Italy
istria-south.why: Italy held Istria by end 1918 (Villa Giusti armistice 3 Nov 1918) but formal cession is Rapallo, 12 Nov 1920 (Wikipedia Treaty of Rapallo; Hrvatska). Rovinj page gives 1918 for Italy, Pula page 1918. Competing SCS claim 1918-20 was diplomatic; Italy held the ground.

istria-south.label: Croatia
istria-south.why: Declaration 25 June 1991, independence effective 8 Oct 1991, recognition Jan 1992 (Wikipedia Independence of Croatia); JNA left Istria 6 Dec 1991 (Hrvatska). No fighting in Istria described.

istria-west.label: Republic of Venice
istria-west.polity: Republic of Venice — Istria da Mar
istria-west.why: Contradicted for THIS ground. Wikipedia Istria: Poreč formally to Venice 15 Feb 1267, Umag 1269, Novigrad 1270, Rovinj 1283; Hrvatska enciklopedija: Poreč 1267, Rovinj 1283, Pula 1331; Wikipedia Poreč 1267 'first Istrian city'; Umag 1269 (Wikipedia Umag); Buje 1358-1797 (Wikipedia Buje). 1331 is Pula's date. Gradual, 1267-1358. No source on rivalry.

istria-west.label: Habsburg / Austria–Hungary
istria-west.why: Campo Formio 17 Oct 1797 gives Istria to Austria (Hrvatska enciklopedija; Wikipedia Buje). End approximate: Pressburg 26 Dec 1805 vs Kingdom of Italy from 1806 (Wikipedia Istria 1806-1810). Wikipedia Umag wrongly says French 1797-1815.

istria-west.label: Napoleonic — Illyrian Provinces
istria-west.why: Contradicted label. Kingdom of Italy included Istria from the Pressburg treaty (26 Dec 1805; annexation announced 30 Mar 1806, ratified 1 May 1806) until it was ceded to France under Schönbrunn (14 Oct 1809), effective 10 June 1810 (Wikipedia Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy); Hrvatska enciklopedija: 1805-1809 Kingdom of Italy, 1809 Illyrian Provinces. Austria returned Oct 1813 / 1814 (Hrvatska). Wikipedia Poreč: Kingdom of Italy then Illyrian Provinces.

istria-west.label: Habsburg / Austria–Hungary
istria-west.why: Start approximate: Austria returned Oct 1813 / Treaty of Paris 1814 (Hrvatska enciklopedija); Wikipedia Poreč '1814', Buje and Umag '1815'. 'Küstenland' anachronistic before 1849 (Kingdom of Illyria 1816-49).

istria-west.label: Italy
istria-west.why: Italy held Istria by end 1918 (Villa Giusti armistice 3 Nov 1918); formal cession Rapallo 12 Nov 1920 (Wikipedia; Hrvatska). Wikipedia Poreč, Buje, Rovinj, Umag all give 1918 for Italian rule.

istria-west.label: Croatia
istria-west.why: Declaration 25 June 1991, effective 8 Oct 1991, recognition Jan 1992 (Wikipedia Independence of Croatia); JNA left Istria 6 Dec 1991 (Hrvatska). The Croatia-Slovenia dispute (Dragonja valley, Piran Bay, 2017 arbitration, Croatia rejects) is on the northern edge; Wikipedia does not name Poreč, Umag, Buje as disputed.

kvarner.label: Habsburg / Austria–Hungary
kvarner.polity: Habsburg — Senj a Military Frontier garrison
kvarner.why: Contradicted. 1469 is Matthias Corvinus's army taking Senj and founding the Senj captaincy (Hrvatska enciklopedija: Senj) - Hungarian-Croatian crown, not Habsburg. Rijeka went to the Habsburgs in 1466 (Wikipedia Rijeka; Hrvatska). Vinodol stayed Frankopan, divided with Zrinski 1577, to the Habsburg crown only in 1671 (Hrvatska Vinodol). Senj returned to the Military Frontier 1776 (Hrvatska Senj). The three grounds differ; contested not assessed (Uskok war with Venice ended 1617, Wikipedia Senj, but no source on who held title).

kvarner.label: Napoleonic — Illyrian Provinces
kvarner.why: Illyrian Provinces created by Schönbrunn 14 Oct 1809 (Wikipedia Illyrian Provinces; Hrvatska Vinodol: 1809-1813). End approximate: Fiume held by the British navy 3 July-26 Aug 1813 then Austrian (Wikipedia list of governors of Fiume); Austria's recovery 1813-14, Treaty of Paris 30 May 1814, Vienna 1815 (Wikipedia Illyrian Provinces); Wikipedia Rijeka infobox gives 1809-1816.

kvarner.label: Yugoslavia
kvarner.why: Partisans entered Rijeka 3 May 1945; Morgan Line placed Rijeka in Yugoslav Zone B (Wikipedia Morgan Line); Paris Peace Treaty 1947 formally ceded it (Hrvatska Rijeka; Wikipedia Rijeka). Rijeka and Sušak merged 1948 (Wikipedia Sušak: council election 1 Feb 1948; Hrvatska says 1947). 1945 de facto vs 1947 de jure.

kvarner.label: Croatia
kvarner.why: Declaration 25 June 1991, effective 8 Oct 1991, recognition Jan 1992 (Wikipedia Independence of Croatia). No source found on the Kvarner situation in 1991, so contested unassessed.

natal.why: Wikipedia's infobox dates the republic 1839; the Boers took control of Port Natal in May 1838

natal.polity: Union of South Africa — Province of Natal

palatinate.polity: Bavaria — the Palatinate (the Rheinkreis, called Pfalz from 1835)
palatinate.why: Bavarian rule followed Napoleon's defeat; the sources give no single year

queensland.label: Britain and its colonies
queensland.why: 1788 is the founding of New South Wales (arrival 18 Jan, colony proclaimed 7 Feb 1788), not of European authority at Moreton Bay: convict settlement there began 1824 (Brisbane site 2 Dec 1824), free settlement allowed 1842. Much of the region's ground (north, west to 138E) was not administered for decades. No rival state claimant found in sources read; Indigenous sovereignty is not discussed in them.

queensland.label: Britain and its colonies
queensland.why: Queensland separation: Letters Patent signed 6 Jun 1859, but the colony was proclaimed in Brisbane 10 Dec 1859, 'separation became a legal reality' only then. Two dates six months apart; Queensland Day marks 6 June but the Queensland State Archives says the colony was born at the proclamation. Until then NSW law applied. The 1862 western boundary move (141E to 138E) is noted, and the 28 deg S border is stated differently in one Archives post (29 deg).

queensland.label: Australia
queensland.why: Commonwealth proclaimed and Queensland became a State on 1 Jan 1901 (Constitution in force); one clean date.

rhenish-hesse.polity: Grand Duchy of Hesse — Rhenish Hesse
rhenish-hesse.why: the department was divided in 1814 and Hesse received it at the Congress of Vienna in 1815

rhenish-hesse.label: Hesse-Darmstadt — the Landgraviate, Grand Duchy and People's State

santafe.polity: Spanish Empire — Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
santafe.why: 1580 is not an event: Santa Fe city was founded 15 Nov 1573 by Garay (Wikipedia, es.wikipedia). The 'Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata' did not exist until 1 Aug 1776; before that the land belonged to the Viceroyalty of Peru. No source found for conditions on the Rosario ground in 1580, so contested is left unassessed.

vojna-krajina.label: Habsburg / Austria–Hungary
vojna-krajina.why: No source gives 1746: Wikipedia says the Slavonian Frontier was established 1745 and the Banat Frontier 1751, with the Vlach Statute abolished 1737; Hrvatska enciklopedija says 'mid-18th century' the captaincies were replaced by 11 regiments and the Military Krajina Rights were issued in 1754. So 1746 is approximate. Habsburg control of the Frontier itself was not disputed in this period, though the Ottomans held Donji Lapac to 1791. Napoleonic note: the Illyrian Provinces 1809-1813 included Croatian lands southwest of the Sava (Wikipedia Illyrian Provinces), which covers Military Croatia. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/vojna-krajina

vojna-krajina.label: Habsburg / Austria–Hungary
vojna-krajina.why: 1848 is a political turning point (serfdom abolished, Jelacic becomes commander, krajisnik representatives demand union with civil Croatia: Hrvatska enciklopedija), not a change of sovereignty. Demilitarisation was gradual: Basic Laws 1850, Transylvanian Frontier 1851/53, Krizevci and Djurdjevac regiments 1 Aug 1871, cordon abolished 1872, Banat Frontier 8 Aug 1873, rest 1881. Command stayed in Vienna, so who held the ground was not in dispute, though Croatian and Hungarian estates claimed it. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Frontier

vojna-krajina.label: Hungary
vojna-krajina.why: Imperial manifesto of incorporation 15 July 1881 (Hrvatska enciklopedija; Wikipedia Military Frontier and Croatia-Slavonia agree), effective 1 Aug 1881; Lika restored to Croatia-Slavonia on 15 July 1881 (Wikipedia: Lika). End 1918: the Croatian Sabor proclaimed independence and joined the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs on 29 Oct 1918 (Wikipedia), union into the Kingdom of SCS 1 Dec 1918. Both within weeks, one year. Banat Frontier (outside the ring) was abolished earlier, 1873. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/vojna-krajina

vojna-krajina.label: Yugoslavia
vojna-krajina.polity: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes; Yugoslavia
vojna-krajina.why: Sabor decision 29 Oct 1918 and union 1 Dec 1918 (Wikipedia: Croatia-Slavonia, Banat/Backa/Baranja page) are in one year; Kingdom of Yugoslavia renamed 3 Oct 1929. End 1941: Axis invasion 6 April 1941, NDH proclaimed 10 April 1941 (Wikipedia). Both clean for the Krajina ground, with the proviso that Srijem was entered by Serbian forces in Nov 1918. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_State_of_Croatia

vojna-krajina.label: Yugoslavia
vojna-krajina.why: Start fuzzy: Srijem liberated only on 12 April 1945 (Syrmian Front), the NDH ended 8-25 May 1945. End 1991: Croatia declared independence 25 June 1991, postponed three months (Brioni 7 July 1991), effective Oct 1991. Within the era the ground was uncontested Yugoslav (SR Croatia/SR Serbia). Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrmian_Front

vojvodina.label: Ottoman Empire
vojvodina.why: Start approximate: Mohacs 1526, but Hrvatska enciklopedija says Srijem was subdued by 1529, Backa by 1540 and Banat by 1551-52. Contested: Jovan Nenad's brief Serb state 1526-27 (Wikipedia, History of Vojvodina). End approximate: Backa and part of Srijem passed to the Habsburgs in 1699 (Karlowitz), the Banat and rest of Srijem only in 1716-1718 (Passarowitz). Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/vojvodina

vojvodina.label: Yugoslavia
vojvodina.polity: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, then Yugoslavia
vojvodina.why: Serbian forces entered Novi Sad 9 Nov 1918, dismantled the Banat Republic (proclaimed 31 Oct) on 15 Nov, assembly voted union with Serbia on 25 Nov 1918, Kingdom of SCS 1 Dec 1918; the exact borders were set by the peace conference: eastern Banat to Romania 1919, northern Backa/Baranya to Hungary 1920 (Wikipedia: Banat, Backa and Baranja). Sovereignty was in question until Trianon. End 1941: Axis invasion 6 April 1941. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banat,_Ba%C4%8Dka_and_Baranja

vojvodina.label: Serbia
vojvodina.polity: Yugoslavia, then Serbia — the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina
vojvodina.why: Start 1944: autumn 1944 for Banat and Backa, April 1945 for Srijem (Syrmian Front breakthrough 12 April 1945). Autonomous province: Hrvatska enciklopedija says delimited from Croatia and joined Serbia as an autonomous province in 1945-46; Wikipedia says 1945. The military administration period was not verified. Since then no competing authority was found. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/vojvodina

western-cape.label: Dutch — the Company and the Batavian Republic
western-cape.why: Sources differ on the year: Wikipedia Cape Colony and Swellendam give British rule 1795 to 1802 (Treaty of Amiens), while the Dutch Cape Colony article gives handover 1 Mar 1803 and Graaff-Reinet article says Feb 1803. No rival authority in the west found.

western-cape.label: Britain and its colonies
western-cape.why: Blaauwberg 8 Jan 1806, capitulation of Cape Town 10 Jan, Batavian army 18 Jan 1806; but Britain's possession was formalised only by the cession of 13 Aug 1814 (Anglo-Dutch convention; Wikipedia Cape Colony says 1814 treaty). De facto 1806, de jure 1814: gap over a year.

western-cape.label: Britain and its colonies
western-cape.why: Union of South Africa came into existence 31 May 1910; Cape Colony ended then.

western-cape.label: South Africa
western-cape.why: Republic of South Africa 31 May 1961 (1961 constitution; left Commonwealth).
